decisionMemo.businessProblem: An HR-tech SaaS company has reassuring blended metrics (30% growth, NPS 45, ~5% quarterly churn) and plans to scale mid-market acquisition and lead its Series B with these numbers. Competing hypotheses: (1) retention is genuinely healthy and scaling mid-market is sound; (2) the blended 5% churn averages a healthy enterprise segment (2%) with a deteriorating mid-market segment (8% and rising over three quarters) that is ~30% of revenue, so the very segment leadership wants to scale is the one with a retention problem - and growing it will mechanically worsen blended churn and unit economics; (3) a mix. The segment churn split is already tracked and visible; what is missing is the WHY of mid-market churn (coded reasons, segment NPS, cohort curves) and the projected blended churn under the planned mix shift.
